newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello sees rates "Santa Claus" by Xmas.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello sees rates "Santa Claus" by Xmas.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello, asked about Australian interest rates, said in New York on Thursday that there was reason enough to expect "Santa Claus" to deliver both this year and next year.
Costello said in New York when asked by reporters about Australian official interest rates that long term rates had fallen and a balanced budget budget was in prospect.
"I think that's reason enough for Santa Claus both this year and next year, I'll say," Costello said. His comments were broadcast on Australian Broadcasting Corp radio on Friday.

"Three and a half percent growth -- not bad -- two percent inflation -- not bad -- balanced budget in three years -- not bad -- a fall of 130 basis points in your long term bond -- not bad," Costello said immediately before his Santa Claus comment.
The Reserve Bank of Australia, which controls monetary policy in consultation with the government, cut official cash interest rates by half a percentage point to 7.00 percent on July 31.
Economists generally expect that official rates will be cut again before the end of the year.
